name: Psychoacoustic Metrics Index
description: An index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics (loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonality, impulsiveness and psychoacoustic annoyance), organised by the standard edition or model each implementation follows. All programming languages.

families.name: Loudness
families.summary: How loud a sound is perceived, in sone (loudness) and phon (loudness level). Four model families are standardised: Zwicker (ISO 532-1), Moore–Glasberg (ISO 532-2), Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3) and the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2).

families.name: Sharpness
families.summary: The sensation produced by high-frequency content, in acum. Standardised in DIN 45692 on top of Zwicker loudness; ECMA-418-2 does not define sharpness.

families.name: Roughness
families.summary: The sensation produced by fast amplitude or frequency modulation (roughly 15 to 300 Hz, strongest near 70 Hz), in asper.

families.name: Fluctuation strength
families.summary: The sensation produced by slow modulation (below about 20 Hz, strongest near 4 Hz), in vacil.

families.name: Tonality
families.summary: How prominent tonal components are. Covers psychoacoustic tonality models (Aures, ECMA-418-2) and the engineering measures used for product noise (tone-to-noise ratio, prominence ratio) and for environmental noise (tonal audibility and tone adjustments).

families.name: Impulsiveness
families.summary: How prominent impulsive sounds are, and the adjustment applied to them in environmental noise assessment.

families.name: Psychoacoustic annoyance
families.summary: Single-number models that combine loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength and, in later models, tonality into a predicted annoyance.

families.name: Related quantities
families.summary: Quantities that psychoacoustic tools often include and that are closely tied to the metrics above.

methods.name: Zwicker loudness
methods.title: Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)
methods.summary: Loudness from Zwicker's model: third-octave band levels are turned into specific loudness on the critical-band (Bark) scale and integrated. ISO 532-1:2017 specifies one procedure for stationary sounds and one for time-varying sounds (from which percentile values such as N5 are taken), and replaced method B of ISO 532:1975. The German standards DIN 45631 (stationary) and DIN 45631/A1 (time-varying) describe the same method.

edition_notes.iso-532-1975: Method B (Zwicker) for stationary sounds, from third-octave levels.
edition_notes.chalupper-fastl-2002: Dynamic loudness model built on Zwicker's model, also for hearing impairment (not standardised).
edition_notes.din-45631-a1-2010: Adds the procedure for time-varying sounds.
edition_notes.iso-532-1-2017: Stationary and time-varying procedures; Annex A reference program, Annex B test signals.
edition_notes.iso-532-1-ed2-draft: Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024.

implementations.scope: stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels
implementations.note: Model tables taken from MoSQITo and checked element by element; one upper-slope value (0.22) follows the ISO 532-1 reference C table where MoSQITo uses 0.24.

implementations.scope: stationary (also per segment and from a spectrum) and time-varying
implementations.note: Validation scripts use the ISO 532-1 Annex B test signals; the documentation marks it as validated.
Written from the Annex A reference program; Annex B test signals are used in the tests.
Compared with SQAT (MATLAB).
Checked with the 25 test signals of Annex B.2–B.5 against the standard's tolerances. Fixes to the time-varying procedure are on `main` only (PR #48).

methods.name: Moore–Glasberg loudness
methods.title: Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)
methods.summary: Loudness of stationary sounds from the Moore–Glasberg model: the spectrum is turned into an excitation pattern on the ERB-number scale, then into specific loudness, which is summed. ANSI S3.4-2007 standardised the model of Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997) with later modifications; ISO 532-2:2017 specifies the method for monaural and binaural listening.

edition_notes.moore-1997: Model paper (thresholds, loudness and partial loudness).
edition_notes.ansi-s3-4-2007: American standard based on the 1997 model with later modifications.
edition_notes.chen-2011: Faster excitation-pattern calculation, also for hearing loss (not standardised).
edition_notes.iso-532-2-2017: Monaural and binaural loudness of stationary sounds; source code supplied with the standard.
edition_notes.iso-532-2-ed2-draft: Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024.

implementations.note: The documentation says it reproduces the Annex B tone and broadband cases to within a percent or two.

methods.name: Time-varying loudness (Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher)
methods.title: Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)
methods.summary: Loudness of time-varying sounds as instantaneous, short-term and long-term loudness. It starts from the Glasberg & Moore (2002) model; Moore et al. (2016) added binaural inhibition and Moore et al. (2018) revised the time constants. ISO 532-3:2023 standardises the resulting Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher method for stationary and time-varying sounds.

edition_notes.glasberg-moore-2002: Time-varying loudness model (short-term and long-term loudness).
edition_notes.iso-532-3-2023: Standardised method; source code supplied with the standard.
edition_notes.iso-532-3-ed2-draft: Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024.

implementations.note: Documented deviations: it runs at the native sample rate instead of resampling to 32 kHz, and the Annex B WAV-file cases are not reproduced (Annex C values are used instead).

methods.name: Sottek Hearing Model loudness
methods.title: Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)
methods.summary: Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model defined in ECMA-418-2. The hearing model (Clause 5) produces specific loudness; the 2nd edition (2022) added a loudness calculation for sounds with tonal and noise components (Clause 8). ECMA-418-2 has had four editions in five years, so implementations of different editions can disagree.

edition_notes.ecma-418-2-ed2: New Clause 8, loudness of sounds with subcritical or wider bandwidth.
edition_notes.ecma-418-2-ed3: Adds a diffuse-field outer and middle ear filter.
edition_notes.ecma-418-2-ed4: Hearing-model clauses 5.1.2.2 and 5.1.5.2 revised; conformance requires 48 kHz sampling.

implementations.scope: Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo
implementations.note: Adapted from the SQAT/RefMap MATLAB code by Lotinga and Torjussen.
Checked at the calibration signal only, where it gives 0.9843 sone_HMS (−1.55 %).
A wrapper that calls sottek-hearing-model.

implementations.scope: mono or stereo, with combined binaural output
implementations.note: Unit tests check the standard's calibration signals (1 kHz, 40 dB gives 1 sone_HMS); the MATLAB code it was translated from was compared with commercial reference software in the paper.
Updated to the 4th edition on `main` in 2025.

implementations.scope: mono or two channels with binaural combination
implementations.note: Checked against equal-loudness contours and against reference results from commercial software on a binaural recording.
Followed the 1st edition (2020) in versions 1.0.0–1.1.1 and the 2nd edition (2022) from 1.2.0. Validation scripts compare with figures of the standard.

methods.name: Sharpness
methods.title: Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)
methods.summary: Sharpness is the weighted first moment of specific loudness along the critical-band rate, with a weighting that emphasises high frequencies. DIN 45692:2009 standardises the weighting and a test procedure, using Zwicker specific loudness (ISO 532-1 / DIN 45631). Most implementations also offer the weightings of von Bismarck (1974) and Aures (1985).

edition_notes.aures-1985-euphony: Weighting that depends on total loudness.
edition_notes.fastl-zwicker-2007: Zwicker & Fastl weighting as given in the textbook.
edition_notes.din-45692-2009: Standardised weighting and test procedure; no revision announced.

implementations.scope: weightings: DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck, Fastl
implementations.note: Validation scripts use the DIN 45692 test signals; the documentation marks it as validated.

implementations.scope: also the informative Aures and von Bismarck variants
implementations.note: Checked with the DIN 45692 reference signal and Table A.2.
Compared with SQAT (MATLAB).

implementations.scope: DIN 45692 weighting, plus von Bismarck and Aures options
implementations.note: Checked with the narrowband and broadband test signals of DIN 45692.

methods.name: Roughness (Daniel & Weber)
methods.title: Roughness, Daniel & Weber model
methods.summary: Roughness from the model of Daniel & Weber (1997), an optimised version of Aures's (1985) model. It is not standardised, and the paper leaves details open (filter bank, calibration, framing), so implementations can give different values for the same signal.
methods.notes: SQAT replaced its implementation in September 2026 with one that follows Dik Hermes's code, which changes results compared with SQAT v1.3 and earlier.

edition_notes.aures-1985-roughness: Earlier model that Daniel & Weber optimised.

implementations.note: Follows SQAT revision `e6228b78`, which includes SQAT's September 2026 rewrite.
The documentation marks it as validated against reference data.
Compared with SQAT v1.3, before SQAT's September 2026 rewrite.

Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature. Rewritten on `main` (PR #65, 2026-09-08) after revised code from Dik Hermes: 63 of 119 validation values go up and 56 down (largest change 0.155 asper).

methods.name: Sottek Hearing Model roughness
methods.title: Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)
methods.summary: Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model, Clause 7 of ECMA-418-2. The 2nd edition (2022) added an optional entropy weighting for cases where rotational speed is measured; the 3rd edition (2024) changed zero-padding and segmentation, the largest change to roughness so far.

edition_notes.ecma-418-2-ed3: Zero-padding and segmentation adapted; main revision of roughness.
edition_notes.ecma-418-2-ed4: Hearing-model and conformance updates (48 kHz sampling).

implementations.scope: mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied
implementations.note: Uses the standard's 20 ms grid and nominal calibration factor, where SQAT uses a slightly adjusted calibration.
Checked at the calibration signal only.
A wrapper that calls sottek-hearing-model.
Amended to the 4th edition on `main` in November 2025.
The documentation still lists it as under development. An open pull request (#95) fixes the low-pass filter range, which caused discrepancies with SQAT for time-varying signals.

methods.name: Roughness (DIN 38455)
methods.title: Roughness, DIN 38455
methods.summary: DIN 38455:2024 is the first German standard for calculating roughness. Its text is not freely available, and the model it specifies could not be confirmed from public sources; a hearing-model roughness was proposed for DIN standardisation by Sottek & Becker (2019).

methods.name: Fluctuation strength (Osses et al.)
methods.title: Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula
methods.summary: Fluctuation strength describes slow modulation around 4 Hz. Osses, García & Kohlrausch (2016) proposed a signal-based model; Fastl & Zwicker give a closed-form expression for modulated tones and noises. Neither is standardised. ECMA-418-2:2025 added a hearing-model method, listed on its own page.

edition_notes.fastl-zwicker-2007: Closed-form expression for amplitude- and frequency-modulated sounds.

implementations.note: Compared with Table 1 of Osses et al. (2016) and with SQAT (correlation 0.98). Validated for amplitude modulation only; a steady 1 kHz tone reads about 0.09 vacil.
Checked against amplitude- and frequency-modulation dependences from the literature.

methods.name: Sottek Hearing Model fluctuation strength
methods.name_zh: Sottek 听觉模型波动强度（ECMA-418-2）
methods.title: Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)
methods.summary: Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model, new in the 4th edition of ECMA-418-2 (June 2025, Clause 9). It uses high-resolution spectral analysis for modulation rates of about 0.25 to 20 Hz.

implementations.note: Checked at the calibration signal only (0.993 vacil_HMS); misprints found in Clause 9 are listed in its errata.

implementations.scope: needs at least 1.37 s of signal; binaural option
implementations.note: Merged on 2026-09-18. A draft report compares it with the MATLAB version (equal to floating-point precision) and with HEAD ArtemiS SUITE v17 (calibration 0.994 vs 1.003 vacil_HMS; recordings −8 % to +12 %). Five departures from the printed equations, judged to be misprints, are documented.
Open pull request since 2026-09-17.

methods.name: Tonality (Aures)
methods.title: Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model
methods.summary: Tonality from Aures (1985): tonal components are extracted with the method of Terhardt, Stoll & Seewann (1982), weighted, and related to the loudness of the whole sound. Not standardised.
methods.notes: SQAT corrected several issues in September 2026 (for example, only the first tonal component entered the weighting), which changes results compared with SQAT v1.3 and earlier.

edition_notes.terhardt-1982: Extraction of tonal components used by the model.

implementations.note: Follows SQAT's September 2026 revision (250 ms Hann windows, 125 ms hop); exact agreement with MATLAB is not established.
A June 2026 commit corrected its calibration; it predates SQAT's September 2026 fixes.

v1.3 is checked with one signal-to-noise comparison. Eight defects were fixed on `main` in September 2026 (for example, only one tonal component's level excess entered the result, and tones were removed from the wrong spectrum), with new checks against Aures's Figs. 5 and 6.
Pull request from April 2026 following the improved Aures metric of Estreder et al. (2023); no maintainer reply.

methods.name: Sottek Hearing Model tonality
methods.title: Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)
methods.summary: Psychoacoustic tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model, Clause 6 of ECMA-418-2, with specific tonality and tonal frequency over time. The method came from ECMA-74 (17th edition, 2019) when ECMA-418-2 was first published in 2020.

edition_notes.ecma-74-ed17: Hearing model and tonality before ECMA-418-2 existed.
edition_notes.ecma-418-2-ed4: Hearing-model and conformance updates (48 kHz sampling).

implementations.note: Checked at the calibration signal only.
A wrapper that calls sottek-hearing-model.
Optional experimental tonal-annoyance weighting (Sottek & Becker, 2019) since 0.1.14.
A verification against Annex B.2 (PR #79) was merged and reverted on 2026-09-21 because the Annex B values of the 2025 edition appear to be out of date.

methods.name: Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio
methods.title: Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)
methods.summary: Tone-to-noise ratio (TNR) and prominence ratio (PR) decide whether a discrete tone is prominent: TNR compares the tone with the noise in its critical band, PR compares the critical band with its neighbours. ECMA-418-1 took the method over from Annex D of ECMA-74 in 2020; its 3rd edition (2024) revised the TNR procedure.

edition_notes.ecma-418-1-ed1: Based on, and mostly identical to, ECMA-74 Annex D.
edition_notes.ecma-418-1-ed2: Maximum tone bandwidth for TNR set to 15 % of the critical band; corrections.
edition_notes.ecma-418-1-ed3: TNR procedure revised for repeatable results across FFT resolutions; terms rewritten.

implementations.note: The "prominent" flag applies the numeric criterion only.
Docstrings say "ECMA 418-1" without an edition; the helper code and the bibliography cite ECMA-74 Annex D (17th edition, 2019). The documentation marks it as available but not validated.

methods.name: Tonal components (DIN 45681)
methods.title: Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)
methods.summary: German method that detects tonal components in noise from narrow-band spectra and derives a tone adjustment for the assessment of noise immissions. DIN 45681:2005 with its corrections of 2005 and 2006 is current.

methods.name: Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)
methods.title: Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)
methods.summary: Engineering method for the audibility of tones in noise, from critical-band analysis of narrow-band spectra. First published as ISO/PAS 20065:2016 and turned into ISO/TS 20065:2022, which notes that the method is not validated below 50 Hz.

edition_notes.iso-ts-20065-2022: Technical specification; adds that the method is not validated below 50 Hz.

implementations.note: Follows the 2016 PAS, not the 2022 TS. Does not apply the A-weighting required by clause 5.3.2.

methods.name: Tonal audibility (ISO 1996-2)
methods.title: Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)
methods.summary: Objective tonal audibility and tone adjustment for environmental noise assessment. ISO 1996-2:2007 gave a method in Annex C; ISO 1996-2:2017 replaced it with an engineering method (Annex J) and a survey method (Annex K).

edition_notes.iso-1996-2-2017: Annex J engineering method and Annex K survey method.

implementations.scope: Annex K survey method and Table J.1; in the `phonometry.environment` namespace

implementations.note: Pull request from May 2022; no maintainer reply.

methods.name: Tonal audibility of wind turbines (IEC 61400-11)
methods.title: Tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)
methods.summary: Tonality analysis in the acoustic noise measurement of wind turbines: tones are identified in narrow-band spectra and their tonal audibility is reported.

methods.name: Impulse prominence
methods.title: Prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)
methods.summary: Objective prominence of impulsive sounds and the corresponding adjustment of the equivalent level in environmental noise assessment: Nordtest method NT ACOU 112 and ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022 (adjustment of 0 to 9 dB). Hearing-model impulsiveness metrics are not standardised and no open implementation is listed.

methods.name: Psychoacoustic annoyance
methods.title: Psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)
methods.summary: Psychoacoustic annoyance (PA) combines percentile loudness N5 with sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength (Widmann 1992; Zwicker & Fastl 1999). More (2010) added tonality and Di et al. (2016) adapted the model for tonal noise. None of these is standardised; ISO/AWI 26573, registered in 2026, covers the assessment of annoyance through listening tests, including prediction models.

implementations.note: No verification routine (README).
No verification routine (README).
Follows Eqs. 16.2–16.4 of Fastl & Zwicker (2007), the textbook form of Widmann's model.
Added on `main` in June 2025; the README describes it as the same model as the Zwicker & Fastl entry under its original attribution.

methods.name: Equal-loudness contours
methods.title: Equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)
methods.summary: Normal equal-loudness-level contours for pure tones in free-field listening. ISO 226:2023 replaced ISO 226:2003; ECMA-418-2:2025 still refers to the 2003 edition.

implementations.note: The docstring gives no edition; it is based on Jeff Tackett's MATLAB code for ISO 226:2003.

methods.name: Perceived noise level and EPNL
methods.title: Perceived noise level, PNLT and EPNL (ICAO Annex 16, 14 CFR Part 36)
methods.summary: Effective perceived noise level for aircraft noise certification: perceived noisiness in noy, the tone-corrected perceived noise level (PNLT) and a duration correction. Defined in ICAO Annex 16, Volume I, and in the US regulation 14 CFR Part 36.

edition_notes.icao-annex-16-vol-1: International standard for aircraft noise certification.

implementations.note: The README says no reference implementation or test signals exist, so it was only cross-checked. Follows Amendment 36-26 (2005).

implementations.scope: PNL, PNLT and EPNL, in the `phonometry.aircraft` namespace
implementations.note: Tested with the EPNL example of ICAO Doc 9501 (Environmental Technical Manual).

methods.name: Aural detectability
methods.title: Aural detectability of sounds in background noise
methods.summary: How likely a listener is to detect a sound in background noise, from signal-to-noise ratios in auditory filters and signal-detection theory. Used for aircraft, drone and urban air mobility noise. Not standardised.

Widely used, but without a release or a commit since April 2024.

paper.citation: San Millán-Castillo, R., Latorre-Iglesias, E., Glesser, M., Wanty, S., Jiménez-Caminero, D., & Álvarez-Jimeno, J. M. (2021). MOSQITO: an open-source and free toolbox for sound quality metrics in the industry and education. *INTER-NOISE 2021*, INCE Conference Proceedings 263(5).

notes: Started by EOMYS in 2020. The default branch is `master`; its last commit and the last release (1.2.1) are both from 2024-04-22.
The documentation lists Soundscapy as a user; several other projects (PsychoBox, Sonemeter and others) wrap it.
Also computes the ANSI S3.5 speech intelligibility index (`sii_ansi`), which is outside the scope of this index.

Open, unanswered pull requests add Aures tonality ([#97](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/97), 2026), ECMA-418-2 roughness fixes ([#95](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/95), 2026) and an ISO 1996-2 Annex K tone detector ([#52](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/pull/52), 2022).
A C#/.NET port, Mosqito.NET, was announced in issue [#98](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/issues/98) (not checked).
caveats: No maintainer has answered issues or pull requests opened since 2024, including bug reports on TNR/PR (#80,
`import mosqito` fails when matplotlib is not installed, because it is imported but not declared as a dependency ([#100](https://github.com/Eomys/MoSQITo/issues/100)); install matplotlib yourself.
Its ECMA-418-2 functions follow the 2nd edition (2022), two editions behind the current one.

notes: The README lists 61 studies and theses that use SQAT. Software DOI (all versions) [10.5281/zenodo.7934709](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7934709).

The ECMA-418-2 functions come from the RefMap MATLAB code by Lotinga and Torjussen (University of Salford).

The README warns that `main` may contain changes that are not yet fully verified and recommends using a release.

updates.title: First public version
updates.body:
The index starts with the projects, methods and standard editions listed on the website. Every
implementation is tied to the edition or model paper it follows, with links to the documentation the
facts were taken from.

Worth knowing as of today:

- ECMA-418-2 is at its 4th edition (June 2025), which added fluctuation strength. Implementations of
  earlier editions are still in use, so check which edition a tool follows before comparing results.
- SQAT's main branch carries unreleased changes to Aures tonality and Daniel & Weber roughness
  (September 2026) that change results compared with SQAT v1.3.
- All three parts of ISO 532 are being revised; committee drafts have existed since November 2024.
- DIN 38455:2024 is the first German standard for roughness. No open implementation is known.
- MetaSona (C library with a Python interface, first released in September 2026) is a new entry.
